conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes 'yes' to the question, citing randomized controlled trial evidence (such as NLST and NELSON) demonstrating that low-dose CT screening reduces lung-cancer mortality among high-risk heavy current and former smokers.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: yes.** Randomized-trial evidence shows that CT-based lung-cancer screening lowers *lung-cancer mortality* among people at high risk because of substantial current or past smoking. Thus, the proposed “no” answer is not supported.

The U.S. National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) randomized 53,454 high-risk participants to low-dose helical CT or chest radiography and found fewer deaths from lung cancer with CT (widely reported as a 20% relative reduction). This is mortality evidence—not merely earlier diagnosis—so it is not explained by lead-time bias. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21714641/

A separate large Dutch-Belgian randomized trial (NELSON), comparing volume low-dose CT screening with no screening in high-risk current and former smokers, corroborated the finding: lung-cancer mortality was significantly lower in the screened group; reported 10-year reductions were 24% in men and 33% in women. https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1911793

The evidence does **not** mean CT screening is beneficial for every smoker or that it prevents lung cancer. It detects some cancers early enough for more effective treatment, while also causing false-positive findings, follow-up testing, radiation exposure, possible overdiagnosis, and anxiety. A Cochrane review synthesized randomized-trial evidence on both mortality and harms. https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD013829.pub2/full

Accordingly, the USPSTF concluded with moderate certainty that annual low-dose CT has a moderate net benefit for people at high risk, and recommends it for adults aged 50–80 with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years, subject to individual health status and shared decision-making. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening
